title: VnExpress Marathon Hai Phong 2026 Review: Racing on a French Colonial Beach Peninsula
seo_title: VnExpress Marathon Hai Phong 2026 Review | Do Son
meta_description: VnExpress Marathon Hai Phong 2026 review: December 13 at Do Son -- a former French colonial resort peninsula, from Vietnam's largest digital newspaper.
dek: Set for 13 December 2026 at Do Son, this VnExpress-organised marathon runs on a peninsula the French turned into a summer resort for their colonial expatriate community.
verdict: The VnExpress Marathon Hai Phong extends the same major-newspaper organisational model covered at VnExpress's Hanoi Midnight race elsewhere in this research batch to Do Son -- a genuinely scenic peninsula 5 kilometres long, formed by the Dragon Mountain Range, that the French colonial administration turned into a summer resort for their expatriate community and the Vietnamese upper class. Four distances from 5K to the full marathon give it broad accessibility. Registration status wasn't yet announced at the time of this research, and no independent participant reviews were found.

sections.heading: The Same Newspaper, a Different City
paragraphs: The race offers four distances -- 5K, 10K, 21.1K and the 42.195K full marathon -- at Do Son, Hai Phong. [1] Like the VnExpress Marathon Hanoi Midnight covered elsewhere in this research batch, this event is organised by VnExpress, Vietnam's largest online newspaper, and FPT Online -- giving it the same broad media promotional reach applied to a different Vietnamese city.

sections.heading: A Former French Colonial Resort
paragraphs: Do Son is a district about 20km southeast of Hai Phong's city centre, formed by a peninsula extending 5km into the sea, created by the Dragon Mountain Range. [2] Upon establishing their presence in Hai Phong, the French turned Do Son into a summer resort for their colonial expatriate community and the Vietnamese upper class -- giving the area genuine historical depth alongside its natural coastal scenery.

sections.heading: Distinct Beach Zones and a Historic Tower
paragraphs: The peninsula's beach area splits into three zones, with Zone II offering the main recreational swimming beach; Zone I has no beach but features rougher waves and rocky terrain. [2] The peninsula's highest point, Tuong Long Tower on Long Son Mountain (95.2m elevation), is a reconstruction of an original tower dating to the Ly Dynasty -- a genuine historical landmark for race weekend sightseeing.

sections.heading: Registration Not Yet Announced
paragraphs: As of this writing, registration status has not been announced. [1] No independent participant reviews were found in research, though VnExpress's massive media reach (demonstrated at its Hanoi event) suggests demand could move quickly once sign-ups open.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If a marathon on a genuinely scenic former-colonial-resort peninsula, backed by one of Vietnam's most-read media outlets, appeals, the VnExpress Marathon Hai Phong on 13 December 2026 is a strong pick. Watch official VnExpress channels for registration to open.
